key_insight: DiffEEG uses self-supervised diffusion pre-training plus reinforcement learning fine-tuning to learn useful EEG representations and improve seizure detection when labels are scarce and events are rare.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support more reliable seizure monitoring in highly imbalanced clinical EEG settings by improving seizure recall without requiring large amounts of labeled data.
method: Pre-trained on 1.3M unlabeled EEG segments with a denoising diffusion model built on a 1D U-Net with multi-head self-attention.
Adapted downstream with a reinforcement learning decision layer optimized to maximize F1-score.
Evaluated with strict patient-wise Leave-One-Fold-Out testing across 279 patients.
evidence_signal: In patient-wise evaluation, DiffEEG reached 81% accuracy and 85% weighted F1 for binary detection, with 59% F1 for 4-class seizure subtyping and 59% seizure recall at 6.7% prevalence.
watch_item: The strong results are from retrospective benchmark evaluation, so clinical deployment would still need external validation and robust real-time testing.
paper_title: DiffEEG: A Self-Supervised Denoising Diffusion Model for Learning EEG Generic Representations
